name: llama.cpp
notable_features: Plain C/C++ with no dependencies, built on the standalone ggml tensor library

ggml is the widest-portability backend set in any LLM engine: CUDA, HIP, MUSA, Metal, SYCL, Vulkan, CANN, OpenCL, WebGPU, OpenVINO (in progress), Hexagon, ZenDNN, RPC, plus CPU NEON/AVX/AVX512/AMX/RVV
Quantization at 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 bits, plus EXL2/EXL3 and NVFP4/MXFP4
CPU+GPU hybrid offload via --n-gpu-layers, including splitting MoE expert weights or dense FFN weights to CPU (--cpu-moe, --n-cpu-moe, --n-cpu-ffn)
llama-server does continuous batching with slot-based parallel decoding and an OpenAI-compatible API
Multiple GPU backends can be compiled into one binary and selected at runtime with --device; backends can also be loaded as shared libraries via GGML_BACKEND_DL
Unified-memory mode (GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1) swaps to system RAM instead of crashing when VRAM is exhausted
hardware_caveats: Vulkan is the universal escape hatch but is not the fast path: it is the only route to a GPU with no vendor SDK, and on Windows it needs the LunarG Vulkan SDK plus w64devkit/MSYS2 plumbing

HIP requires you to name GPU_TARGETS at build time (e.g. -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100) or the build compiles for every GPU present; unsupported gfx versions need HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION, which AMD does not support on Windows
NVFP4 and MXFP4 layers marked W4A16 request 8-bit activations, so on Blackwell they silently run the W4A8 path rather than native W4A4. GGML_CUDA_MMQ_PREC=q4 forces native W4A4 at an accuracy cost

MMQ (the custom quantized matmul kernel) is off by default on GPUs without int8 tensor cores - that is V100, CDNA and RDNA3+ - so quantized models on those parts fall back to slower paths unless GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ is set
CUDA non-native builds (-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF) cover all CUDA GPUs but compile slowly and may still need JIT; otherwise nvcc silently defaults arch when it cannot detect your GPU

On Windows on ARM, MSVC compiles the ARM NEON intrinsics incompletely, so a CUDA build made entirely with MSVC has a slower CPU backend; the release workflow splits the build between clang (CPU) and MSVC (CUDA)
OpenVINO backend is explicitly marked In Progress for Intel CPUs, GPUs and NPUs; SYCL is the maintained Intel GPU path
The SYCL note also warns that the Intel oneMKL/oneAPI CPU build config does not support Intel GPU - use the SYCL path for that
Unified memory hurts performance on non-integrated GPUs while being what makes integrated GPUs usable at all
best_for: Running a quantized GGUF on whatever GPU you happen to own, including GPUs with no vendor compute SDK
Single-user or small-group local serving where install simplicity and low memory use matter more than multi-tenant throughput
Hybrid CPU+GPU inference for models larger than your VRAM
Apple Silicon, which the project treats as a first-class target optimized via NEON, Accelerate and Metal
avoid_for: High-concurrency datacenter serving where a specialized paged-KV engine will schedule better
Squeezing the last FLOP out of a Blackwell or Hopper part - the default W4A8 fallback for W4A16 4-bit layers is a concrete example
Maximum prompt-processing throughput on very old or low-end NVIDIA parts without tuning GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ / GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS
notes: Scheduling: llama-server does implement continuous batching with slot-based parallel decoding, and the server exposes prompt-cache reuse for shared prefixes, but there is no paged-KV block manager in the vLLM sense - KV is allocated per slot from a preallocated pool. 'exl2'/'exl3' are recorded from the project's published support for those quant families; the GGUF variants (Q4_K_M, IQ2_XS, IQ4_XS, UD-Q2_K_XL, TQ1_0/TQ2_0 ternary) are the primary path. safetensors support exists via converters rather than as a native load path.
